summary: Proceed with no companion. The saving is real but is mostly not where the hypothesis puts it. rega_gather's 169-184 us at first_turn is dominated by ~115k dead CTAs (capacity 8T+480 slots, n_padded ~16.6k), not by a 1.5 TB/s copy, so a persistent fused kernel should save ~150-180 us/ft shape and ~30 us/turn_4. The single run reads cleanly on the three profile rows. Its one real performance risk is the fixed 132*8 persistent grid exceeding the resident CTA count.
justification: Profile data on master (bff8e36788a04917.profile.txt) confirms the rows. rega_gather_kernel is 180.6/183.8/180.4/168.9 us on the four first_turn shapes, 28.0/27.6 at turn_4 and 7.1/6.8 at turn_1. at::native vectorized_layer_norm is 76.5-78.5 us at ft and 18.0 at sliding turn_4; at turn_1 it is outside the top list. The mechanism is better than stated. Master's own prepare log shows rega_gather at T=8192 'local' (65536 active slots, ~1.07 GB r+w) taking 276 us eager, about 3.9 TB/s, while T=16384 random (16368 active slots, 268 MB) takes 166 us. The copy itself is therefore near bandwidth, and ~100-110 us of the ft row is the launch/retire cost of ~115k CTAs that only read n_padded and exit (one 256-thread CTA per capacity slot). A persistent grid bounded by the device-side n_padded removes that cost. Folding the norm in also removes a full 268 MB round trip (the 77 us norm row at ~3.5 TB/s), because the fused kernel moves the same ~268 MB the gather already moves: T local-route rows read plus written. A target of ~70-90 us fused vs ~255 us pair at ft (ratio ~0.3) and ~10-15 us vs ~46 us at turn_4 is physically reachable. The 0.90x gate should pass at ft and turn_4, and may be marginal at turn_1 (L2-resident, latency-bound). The expected directions match TASK weights: ft rows -1 to -1.6%, turn_4 ~-1%, turn_1 flat. The headline (~+1%) sits inside the +/-1.5% CI, so the result must be read on rows: vectorized_layer_norm + rega_gather_kernel vs _norm_gather_kernel per shape, plus the prepare GATE lines. WEAKEST LINK: the fixed persistent grid of 132*8 = 1056 programs at num_warps=8 assumes 8 resident 256-thread CTAs per SM, which needs <= 32 registers/thread. A BLOCK=4096 row (16 fp32 per thread), w_eff (another 16 unless re-loaded), the reduction and the address math will likely compile to 40-64 regs, giving 4-6 resident CTAs/SM. Then ~25-50% of the programs start only after the first resident set finishes its whole slot loop, a 1.5-2x tail on a kernel whose whole point is bandwidth. Size the grid from the compiled kernel's n_regs/occupancy (132 * resident CTAs/SM), or sweep the grid multiplier {2,4,8} and num_warps {4,8} inside the existing prepare gate and print each. Secondary: each loop iteration has a dependent scalar chain (block_experts -> sorted_ids -> row load), so per-program memory parallelism is one 8 KB row. That is fine only if residency is high, which is another reason to size the grid by occupancy, not by a constant.
confounders: align-two-phase-all-t-rega (landed, master): it produces sorted_ids/block_experts/n_padded with local-only blocks at BSM 16, which is why n_padded ~ T+pad while capacity stays 8T+480. That ratio creates the dead-CTA cost this change removes. If a later align change shrank sorted_ids capacity to n_padded, rega_gather would get cheaper on its own and this hypothesis's margin would shrink. This is not a confound for this run, because the fused kernel consumes exactly the same align outputs.

experts-turn-rega-s4-port-t4096 / experts-turn-rega-s4-first-turn-n128 (landed): they define rega_gather and the xs contract (zeros at sentinel slots of local blocks, untouched elsewhere). The fused kernel must keep that write set, which the canary check covers. They are the base, not an interaction.

sglang-pipeline-parity (landed): it defines state['pre_expert_norm'] as MuseSpark1xRMSNorm(1+w). The fused kernel's numerics depend on matching that module's formula order and weight dtype, which the getsource print plus the ulp/relL2 gate checks. Matching is a correctness question, not an A/B one.

stack-tonight-five-prefill (landed: router hilo, align, w2 zero-store, Marlin silu): disjoint kernels. zero_nonlocal_w2 only changes y's allocation in _experts_rega, not xs, so there is no interaction.
interference: No companion is warranted. Every replaced kernel has its own row in the archived profile (rega_gather_kernel at all shapes, vectorized_layer_norm at ft and turn_4), and the new _norm_gather_kernel will show as its own row, so a gain or a loss is attributable from this single scored run without a revert. The prepare GATE lines carry an in-process cold-L2 graph A/B per class, and a slow result turns the class OFF and runs master's path byte-identical. One sub-change could in principle be isolated: a persistent grid alone (dead-CTA removal) vs norm fusion. That split is a design question for a follow-up and is not needed to interpret this result. Spending a scored run on it is not justified. Collisions with in-flight work: (a) experts-rega-pingpong-consumers-all-t and experts-rega-producer-scale-expand-all-t both edit _experts_rega, but only the two rega_gemm call sites (rega_gemm -> rega_gemm_pp/sx under a per-class flag). This change edits only the rega_gather call and adds a prenorm argument. The functions are independent at run time (the GEMMs read xs, whatever produced it), and a later stack needs a small hand merge in _experts_rega and at prepare's tail, where all three append post-rega phases and PATH CHOSEN lines. (b) fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated touches only the attention section of kernel_fn, so its hunk is disjoint from the pre-expert norm call site. (c) Deadline: master's prepare totals 124.4 s with the ft phase starting at ~119.9 s, and the new gate runs after _rega_setup returns. It cannot move the REGA_FT_START_DEADLINE_S (150 s) check, REGA_BUDGET_S (200 s) or REGA_COPY_DEADLINE_S (255 s) of this build. It adds ~5-20 s to the total (3 Triton compiles plus 21 x 2 graph replays x 3 classes plus self-checks), well under the 300 s prepare limit. When stacked with the v3 rega builds, its phase must stay after _rega_setup, so it also cannot push their ft start; add a self-imposed skip (e.g. if prepare already used > 270 s, leave every class OFF) so a slow v3 stack cannot push prepare past 300 s.
rules_flags: Weight precision: 'keep its dtype' for the effective (1 + w) weight is fine only if that is the bf16 tensor the module itself holds. If _get_effective_weight() returns fp32, storing an fp32 copy of a BF16 checkpoint weight is a widened weight and was flagged in prior reviews. Preferred: store the bf16 checkpoint w (lossless) and add 1 in fp32 inside the kernel, as turn-align-sglang32-prenorm-triton-restack did. If the module's own forward uses a bf16-rounded (1+w), store exactly that bf16 tensor. Either way, match whichever form getsource shows.

kernel_fn branch duplication: the change re-derives _experts's dispatch condition in kernel_fn. It must be exactly the same shape-only predicate: REGA_MIN_TOKENS < T <= MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS with rega_ok[low|high], or MARLIN_MAX_TOKENS < T <= REGA_FT_MAX with rega_ok['ft']. Otherwise a T that _experts sends to ssdq/Marlin/Triton would receive un-normalized x. Safer to put the branch inside _experts (pass raw x plus a prenorm flag) so there is one predicate. Keep it free of host syncs, prints and try/except.

Triton specialization: any int argument besides num_routes (none should exist; n_padded must stay a pointer) must be do_not_specialize, and every class must be compiled in prepare, so no JIT happens inside the timed call or a graph capture.

No caching from inputs: the per-slot norm is recomputed per call (tokens with several local routes are normalized once per slot). That is allowed and deterministic. Do not memoize per-token rstd across calls.
BF16 activations: xs stays bf16 with one rounding after the norm, the same rounding point as SGLang (norm output bf16, gathered). OK.
open_questions: What do the compiled kernel's n_regs and CTAs/SM come out to at num_warps=8, BLOCK=4096? If fewer than 8 CTAs/SM, the 132*8 grid has a tail. Print it and size the grid by occupancy.

_rega_case has no 'soft' kind: it falls through to _ssdq_case's default (random routing), which is what master's GATE 'ft T=16384 soft' line already uses. Use 'random' (and 'skewed') explicitly so the log is not misleading.

Is _get_effective_weight() for MuseSpark1xRMSNorm bf16 or fp32, and does the forward compute (x*rstd)*w or x*(rstd*w)? The getsource print answers both. Record it in the attempt file before reading the ulp line.

At turn_1 (T=753, ~1.2k active slots of ~6.5k capacity) the pair is ~12 us and L2-resident. Expect the 0.90x gate to pass narrowly or fail. Either outcome is fine, but read turn_1 as 'flat by design'.

Follow-up if this lands: the same dead-CTA pattern may exist in other one-CTA-per-capacity-slot kernels on the rega path (e.g. any scatter or zero-fill keyed by num_slots). Worth a grep before minting the next row-level hypothesis.
